messages.author: b63e01cd28805f12
messages.subject: ggplot object
parts:
Hi community, 

I have a doubt definition ggplot object 

What is a ggplot object? Is it a graphic?

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: ggplot object
parts:
It is a list:

> tmp <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y=mpg)) + geom_point()
> class(tmp)
[1] "gg" "ggplot"
> typeof(tmp)
[1] "list"
> names(tmp)
[1] "data" "layers" "scales" "mapping" "theme"
[6] "coordinates" "facet" "plot_env" "labels"
> tmp$layers
[[1]]
geom_point: na.rm = FALSE
stat_identity:
position_identity: (width = NULL, height = NULL)

> class(tmp$layers)
[1] "list"
> class(tmp$layers[[1]])
[1] "proto" "environment"

HTH,
Ista

messages.author: b63e01cd28805f12
messages.subject: Re: ggplot object
parts:
Thanks Ista, 

phrases: 

"ggplot () Initializes a ggplot object" and "add layers to the Existing ggplot object." of  

> ??ggplot

What do they mean? 

class is ggplot 
type list 

but generates a graph, constructs a graph, graph list and returns



> ??ggplot

ggplot {ggplot2} R Documentation
Create a new ggplot plot

Description

ggplot() initializes a ggplot object. It can be used to declare the input data frame for a graphic and to specify the set of plot aesthetics intended to be common throughout all subsequent layers unless specifically overridden.

Details

ggplot() is typically used to construct a plot incrementally, using the + operator to add layers to the existing ggplot object. This is advantageous in that the code is explicit about which layers are added and the order in which they are added. For complex graphics with multiple layers, initialization with ggplot is recommended.



ggplot() initializes a ggplot object

add layers to the existing ggplot object.














2014-01-30 Ista Zahn <ista...@gmail.com>:

It is a list:

> tmp <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y=mpg)) + geom_point()
> class(tmp)
[1] "gg"     "ggplot"
> typeof(tmp)
[1] "list"
> names(tmp)
[1] "data"        "layers"      "scales"      "mapping"     "theme"
[6] "coordinates" "facet"       "plot_env"    "labels"
> tmp$layers
[[1]]
geom_point: na.rm = FALSE
stat_identity:
position_identity: (width = NULL, height = NULL)

> class(tmp$layers)
[1] "list"
> class(tmp$layers[[1]])
[1] "proto"       "environment"

HTH,
Ista
